Define ADADAS.AVISIT / MT.ADADAS.AVISIT and workbook Methods!D7 refer to SAP Section 8.2; ADRG page-8 supplies no numeric window limits or missing-day assignment. The obs case expression therefore adds conditions absent from the governing retained text, while the shared SAP remains pending_review in the source manifest.

Define ADADAS.AVISIT enumerates Week 8 as a valid label but does not direct creation of an imputed ACTOT visit in locf8. MT.ADADAS.DTYPE and ADRG pages 30-33 identify imputation and distinguish current R-generated rows from historical rows without stating that complete visit-creation rule.

Define ADADAS.AVISIT enumerates Week 16, and ADRG page-32 illustrates a current R-generated Week 16 carry, but neither states a general locf16 visit-creation condition. MT.ADADAS.DTYPE labels imputed records after their eligibility has been determined.

Define ADADAS.AVISIT enumerates Week 24 and ADRG page-14 names a Week 24 LOCF analysis, but neither states when locf24 creates a missing ACTOT analysis visit. ADRG pages 30-33 do not provide a complete general creation rule.

MT.ADADAS.AVISIT and workbook Methods!D7 refer to SAP Section 8.2 without providing the window table; ADRG page-8 supplies only the date/window principle. The source manifest leaves the shared SAP pending_review, so it cannot establish the missing boundaries and imputed-visit conditions.

MT.ADADAS.DTYPE and CL.DTYPE describe ACTOT imputation and LOCF, but do not specify the DONOR8 ANL01FL eligibility filter and analysis-visit ordering. ADRG pages 31-32 illustrate the current selected donor without generalizing those choices or the remaining tie policy.

Original Define VL.ADADAS.AVAL binds WC.ADADAS.PARAMCD.EQ.ACTOT to MT.ADADAS.AVAL.ACTOT (lines 98-101 and 4469-4474), also bound by workbook ValueLevel!D16/O16 and Methods!D6, so the generic QS copy cannot cover all parameters. That method leaves missing-score adjustment to SAP Section 14.2, while the pending_review SAP and ADRG pages 30-33 do not complete that rule or LOCF donor eligibility.

MT.ADADAS.CHG and workbook Methods!D10 give AVAL - BASE without the ABLFL exclusion used by adadas.yaml CHG. ADRG page-33 concerns historical ACTOT/LOCF values and does not document suppressing baseline-flagged change.
MT.ADADAS.PCHG and workbook Methods!D12 give 100* (CHG/BASE) without either the ABLFL exclusion or the BASE <> 0 guard used by adadas.yaml PCHG. ADRG page-33 adds no such condition.

Define ADADAS.PCHG / MT.ADADAS.PCHG and workbook Methods!D12 state the division but no result when BASE is zero; the reported literal execution fails on that arithmetic case. Neither ADRG page-33 nor the original method bindings supply the missing convention, so adding a zero guard would select an undocumented result.

MT.ADADAS.ANL01FL and workbook Methods!D4 document choosing the closest visit, but not the obs signed-distance tie order, null ordering, or remaining-tie choice. ADRG page-8 and pages 31-32 do not specify these additional ranking conventions.

MT.ADADAS.ANL01FL and workbook Methods!D4 describe flagging the chosen visit when multiple visits share a window. They do not state the obs singleton-window flag or its empty-string assignments, and ADRG pages 31-32 give examples rather than a complete general rule.

MT.ADADAS.ANL01FL discusses closest-visit selection without stating that every generated locf8 row receives Y. ADRG pages 31-32 do not establish a general flag assignment for all imputed ACTOT visits.

MT.ADADAS.ANL01FL does not state the unconditional Y assignment to every locf16 row. ADRG page-32 shows Y on a current R-generated Week 16 carry, but that single example does not specify the complete generated-record flag policy.

MT.ADADAS.ANL01FL and workbook Methods!D4 do not state the unconditional Y assignment to every locf24 row. ADRG pages 30-33 discuss imputed ACTOT differences without giving that general assignment rule.

MT.ADADAS.ANL01FL and workbook Methods!D4 specify nearest-visit selection only for multiple visits, leaving singleton, tied/missing-distance, and generated-row cases unstated. Those gaps remain even with published visit/day/target inputs, and ADRG pages 8, 13 and 30-33 do not complete them.

MT.ADADAS.DTYPE and workbook Methods!D11 label an already imputed ACTOT record but do not specify the locf8 no-hit/nonmissing-donor eligibility condition. ADRG pages 30-33 distinguish direct QS rows from imputation without defining complete creation eligibility.

MT.ADADAS.DTYPE and workbook Methods!D11 do not state the locf16 no-hit/nonmissing-donor filter. ADRG page-32 illustrates an eligible current Week 16 carry but does not give the general creation condition.

MT.ADADAS.DTYPE and workbook Methods!D11 do not state the locf24 no-hit/nonmissing-donor filter. ADRG page-14 names the Week 24 LOCF analysis and pages 30-33 discuss differences without supplying that eligibility rule.

CL.DTYPE names Last Observation Carried Forward, but MT.ADADAS.DTYPE does not state the ANL01FL eligibility filter, analysis-visit ordering and tie conventions in DONOR8. ADRG pages 31-32 illustrate a current donor while separately showing historical rows, and do not generalize the selection algorithm.

MT.ADADAS.DTYPE and workbook Methods!D11 require knowing which ACTOT rows are imputed without fully defining their creation and donor eligibility. ADRG pages 30-33 distinguish current R-generated from historical CDISC records, but the examples and retained QS sequence cannot independently classify every carried row.
